observations: The release app was launched first from the build bundle and then directly from the read-only mounted DMG, with isolated data and port 18766.
In both runs the packaged sidecar listened on 127.0.0.1:18766 and returned a valid local-only health response.
The dzmm-next-desktop process stayed alive, but System Events reported zero windows and CoreGraphics had no DZMM window to capture; activating the bundle identifier did not change that state.
Temporary diagnostics confirmed that setup found the configured main WebView; explicitly creating a second diagnostic WebView also produced no WindowServer window. The diagnostic code was removed.
The DMG app and sidecar were quit cleanly after the check, the image was detached, and no process remained on the isolated port.

separate_fix.problem: Vite selected IPv6 localhost while tauri.conf waited on 127.0.0.1:5182, so tauri dev never launched the desktop binary.
separate_fix.change: vite.config now binds 127.0.0.1 explicitly and uses strictPort; tauri dev progressed to the native DevCommand after the change.

assessment: This is a P0 package-player-entry failure on the current macOS machine; a healthy Host is not acceptance evidence for a visible app.
A Tauri upstream report describes a similar macOS 26 GUI lifecycle failure, but it uses newer Tauri/tao and macOS versions, so the shared root cause is an inference rather than confirmed.
A later isolated dependency experiment is recorded separately in phase107; phase106 itself intentionally left the product dependency versions unchanged.
not_proven: Whether the same DMG opens a native window on macOS 14 or 15.
Whether a future Tauri/tao release resolves macOS 26.3.1.
Windows native and Android physical-device package journeys remain unrun.
